title: Neural Network Fundamentals
description: Layers, activations, gradients, and core deep-learning concepts.

questions.prompt: In a basic artificial neuron, what is typically applied to the weighted input sum?
questions.explanation: The activation transforms the weighted sum and enables nonlinear functions when chosen nonlinearly.

questions.prompt: For input x, what does the ReLU activation compute?
questions.explanation: ReLU returns zero for negative inputs and the input itself for positive values.

questions.prompt: Stacking only linear layers without nonlinear activations is equivalent to one linear transformation.
questions.explanation: Compositions of linear maps remain linear, so depth alone adds no nonlinear expressive power.

questions.prompt: What does backpropagation efficiently compute?
options: Gradients of a loss with respect to model parameters
questions.explanation: Backpropagation applies the chain rule through a computation graph to obtain parameter gradients.

questions.prompt: Which are represented in a neural-network computation graph?
options: A proof that the model generalizes
questions.explanation: The graph captures operations and dependencies; generalization is an empirical property, not encoded as a proof.

questions.prompt: Why is the chain rule central to training multilayer networks?
options: It combines local derivatives along composed operations
questions.explanation: Each layer contributes a local derivative, and chain-rule products propagate sensitivities through the network.

questions.prompt: What is a common effect of vanishing gradients in very deep networks?
questions.explanation: Gradients that shrink through many layers make it difficult to update parameters far from the output.

questions.prompt: Which symptom can indicate exploding gradients?
options: Unstable, extremely large updates or loss values
A perfectly flat validation curve only
The model has too few layers
questions.explanation: Large gradient magnitudes can create destabilizing parameter steps and numerical overflow.

questions.prompt: Why can a saturated sigmoid activation impede learning?
options: Its derivative becomes very small at extreme inputs
questions.explanation: Sigmoid derivatives approach zero at large positive or negative inputs, reducing gradient flow.

questions.prompt: Softmax is typically applied across a class dimension to turn logits into normalized class probabilities.
questions.explanation: Softmax exponentiates scores and normalizes them along the selected axis.

questions.prompt: What are logits in a classification network?
options: Unnormalized class scores before probability conversion
questions.explanation: Logits are raw output scores; softmax or another decision rule can transform them for prediction.

questions.prompt: Which are established neural-network initialization approaches?
options: All weights set to the same constant
Random initialization scaled for activation behavior
questions.explanation: Xavier and He methods scale random weights to support signal propagation; identical constants can break neuron symmetry.

questions.prompt: What does batch normalization generally normalize during training?
questions.explanation: Batch normalization uses minibatch statistics during training and running statistics for inference.

questions.prompt: Layer normalization typically normalizes features within each example rather than relying on other examples in a batch.
questions.explanation: Layer normalization computes statistics over feature dimensions for each sample, making it useful for variable batch sizes.

questions.prompt: What does an identity skip connection add in a residual block?
options: The block input to its transformed output
The labels to the input tensor
A new optimizer for every layer
questions.explanation: Residual addition gives a direct signal path around a transformation and can ease optimization.

questions.prompt: What does parameter sharing mean in a convolutional layer?
options: The same kernel weights are applied at many spatial positions
Every image uses a separate model
Each pixel has a unique class label
questions.explanation: A convolution reuses each filter across locations, reducing parameters and expressing translation-equivariant patterns.

questions.prompt: Which methods can regularize neural networks?
options: Increasing training loss by corrupting labels
questions.explanation: Dropout, weight decay, and label-preserving augmentation can reduce overfitting; corrupt labels harm supervision.

questions.prompt: What is one epoch in standard supervised training?
options: One pass through the training dataset
questions.explanation: An epoch denotes processing the complete training set once, often in multiple minibatches.

questions.prompt: A model usually needs to compute parameter gradients during ordinary prediction.
questions.explanation: Inference computes outputs; gradients are normally disabled to save memory and computation.

questions.prompt: Why save a training checkpoint?
options: To resume or restore a particular model and optimizer state
To store the dataset labels publicly
questions.explanation: Checkpoints preserve a training state or selected model version for recovery and reproducibility.
